heros.infro: Roman historian who wrote a monumental history of Rome, Ab Urbe Condita, from its founding through the reign of Augustus in Livy's own time.
heros.name: Livy

heros.infro: Ben Jonson fought the Spaniards in Flanders, returned to England and joined an acting company, and was a member of the Lord Chamberlain's company with William Shakespeare. Human nature fascinated both playwrights, but Jonson specialized in satires like Volpone ("The Fox"). He also wrote masques and poetry, and his fellow writers esteemed him as "O Rare Ben Jonson".
heros.name: Ben Jonson

heros.infro: Raja Raja Cholal was a great emperor of the Tamil Chola Empire in India. He conquered southern India as far as Sri Lanka and Kalinga to the North. He divided the country into districts to help the administration and built the Brihadisvara Temple and enabled wealth distribution.
heros.name: Raja Raja Cholal

heros.infro: Brian mac Cennétig was called Brian Bóruma or Brian Boru. Leader of the Dal Cais dynasty, he made himself king of Munster and subjugated Leinster in Southern Ireland. After overthrowing the Uú Néill dynasty that had reigned over most of Ireland for 300 years, Boru became the last High King of Ireland in 1011. In the 1014 battle of Clontarf when his army fought the armies of Dublin, Leinster, and Norse settlers, Brian Boru was slain although his forces won the day.
heros.name: Brian Boru

heros.infro: Hungry for power, Sforza became the Duke of Milan by seizing power from the rightful heir to the crown after the assassination of his brother Galeazzo.  Although his methods may be less than honorable, Sforza is a firm but able leader.
heros.name: Ludovico Sforza

heros.infro: Lothair III was a powerful and very successful ruler of Saxon descent.  He gained the title of Holy Roman Emperor,in part through a very amicable and beneficial relationship with Pope Innocent II.  His most important long-term contribution to the history of the Germanic lands was in his maintenance of the neglected areas of Saxony in the Northeast where he appointed a number of capable Dukes and lesser magistrates who governed the region effectively.
heros.name: Lothair III, Holy Roman Emperor

heros.infro: Eric IV was king of Denmark from 1241 until his death. His rule is known for bitter conflicts and civil wars against his brothers. At the same time Erik faced trouble from the religious orders who insisted that they were immune from taxes that Erik wanted to assess. Erik wanted the church lands taxed as any other landholder would be. He fought constant wars in an attempt to impose more and more taxes on more and more people.
heros.name: Eric IV of Denmark

heros.infro: Roger de Montgomerie, one of William the Conqueror's principal counselors, was granted the title of Earl of Shrewsbury in 1071 and was charged with the rule of Shropshire, a region to the West of modern day Birmingham making him one of the most powerful magnates in all of England at the time.  His mandate was to prevent Welsh incursions into English lands.
heros.name: Earl of Shrewsbury
